govdocs-archive_org-nsia-BrewerJohnnyCal: Mike Blackwell’s interview with Johnny Calvin Brewer is a JFK-case witness interview. Brewer pointed police to the Texas Theatre where Oswald hid. Witness voices matter. The file belongs to the assassination archive. The item is a fragment of the record.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-OrangeCountyCA_: Michael Granberry’s Orange County College to Teach JFK Conspiracies is a Los Angeles Times piece. The course brought the debate to campus. Students packed the class. The file belongs to the press archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-Pacifica_Pacifi: Harold Weisberg’s letter to Pacifica Radio — July 9, 1974 — is a researcher’s note. Pacifica aired the dissenting voices. The letter may hold a clue. The file belongs to the press archive. The item is a fragment of correspondence.
letters-from-america: The young English poet Rupert Brooke toured North America and the Pacific in 1913, sending home these sparkling letters. He writes about New York, the Canadian wilderness, and the South Seas with a poet's eye and a traveler's delight. Published after his early death in the war, the letters preserve a gifted writer discovering the wider world.
an-introduction-to-the-mortuary-customs-: Smithsonian ethnologist H. C. Yarrow compiled this pioneering study of how Native American peoples honored their dead. Burial mounds, scaffold burials, cremation, and mourning rites across many tribes are described from field reports and museum collections. Though written in the language of its time, it remains a foundational record of Indigenous funeral traditions.
people-of-africa: Edith How introduces young readers to the peoples of Africa — their homes, customs, and ways of life — in simple, respectful prose. Written as a children's geography, it aimed to broaden horizons in an age of empire. Today it reads as a period piece, interesting for what it tried to teach.
first-footsteps-in-east-africa: Richard Burton — explorer, linguist, and Victorian daredevil — recounts his perilous 1854 journey to Harar, the forbidden Muslim city in East Africa. Disguised and alone, he became one of the first Europeans to enter it and live. A classic of exploration literature, thrilling and erudite by turns.
the-french-in-the-heart-of-america: John Finley traces the French in the heart of America — explorers, missionaries, and settlers from the Great Lakes to Louisiana. His eloquent narrative honors France's role in the New World. A beautiful piece of historical writing. Marquette, La Salle, and the coureurs de bois stride through these eloquent, admiring pages.
the-poetical-works-of-oliver-wendell-hol: The doctor-poet's medical poems fill this third volume — verse on healing, the body, and the mysteries of life and death. Holmes the physician speaks through Holmes the poet with unique authority. A rare blend of science and song. No other poet ever wrote so well of the doctor's calling.
the-englishwoman-in-america: Isabella Bird's Englishwoman in America collects her sharp, lively letters from the New World — Canada and the United States as seen by fearless eyes. Her observations entertain and enlighten on every page. The first of her travel classics, and a delightful one.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-africa: A 1913 entry on Africa — the continent's Catholic missions and history. Alexandre Le Roy surveys the vast field. From Augustine's Hippo to the new missions. Martyrs' blood watered the soil. The Church's youngest continent. Its white martyrs crown the modern missions.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-agostino-cias: This 1913 reference piece on Agostino Ciasca — the Augustinian cardinal and orientalist. Giuseppe Balestri honors his learning. His Syriac studies served the Church. Rome prized his eastern lore. A scholar in the Sacred College. His Bible manuscripts enriched the Vatican. His red hat crowned a scholar's life.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alvar-nunez-c: This 1913 reference piece on Cabeza de Vaca — the shipwrecked wanderer of North America. Adolph Bandelier tells his amazing trek. Eight years afoot from Florida to Mexico. His tale opened the Spanish north. The continent's strangest journey. His Naufragios told the incredible tale.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ambrosian-bas: A 1913 entry on the Ambrosian Basilica — Sant'Ambrogio, Milan's mother church. Maurice Hassett describes its ancient glory. The saint's bones rest beneath its altar. Its atrium breathes the fourth century. Milan's holiest ground. Its mosaics gleam with ancient gold. Its pulpit is a Roman sarcophagus.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-america: A 1913 entry on America — the continent's discovery and evangelization. Adolph Bandelier tells the vast story. Cross and crown came together. The missions spanned two hemispheres. The New World's Catholic epic. Its missions are the Church's epic. Its story fills the mission annals.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-angelo-rocca: This 1913 reference article on Angelo Rocca — the Augustinian founder of the Angelica Library. Nicholas Weber honors his gift to Rome. His books opened to all readers. The first public library of the city. A friar's bequest to learning. Its doors opened to every scholar.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-apiarius-of-s: This 1913 reference article on Apiarius of Sicca — the priest of the appeal controversy. John Bertram Peterson tells his tangled case. His appeals vexed popes and councils. Africa's discipline was at stake. A footnote to the papal primacy. His case reached three Roman councils.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-arca: A 1913 entry on the arca — the sacred chest of the old Church. Maurice Hassett describes its holy use. Relics rested within its boards. The faithful venerated the sealed coffer. The treasure chest of the shrine. Its lid bore the carved saints.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-barca: This 1913 reference piece on Barca — the Cyrenaican city, now a titular see. Louis Petit notes its ancient fame. Its bishops grace the old lists. The desert guards its ruined site. A see of the Libyan coast. Its ruins dot the Green Mountain.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-bartholomew-o: This 1913 reference article on Bartholomew of Bragança — a Dominican churchman of note. William Devlin records his career. The entry preserves his modest fame. His order honors its learned sons. A friar in the Church's service. His order honors its learned son.

This 1913 reference piece on Ptolemy of Lucca — the Dominican who wrote the Church's story — honors his pen. Thomas Schwertner wrote it up. His annals run through the medieval years. The friars prized their chronicler. A brother with a historian's care. His chronicle ends with the eighth Boniface.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-bartolommeo-p: A 1913 entry on Cardinal Pacca — Pius VII's loyal minister. Umberto Benigni honors his Napoleonic trials. He shared the pope's captivity. His Memoirs told the stormy years. The Church's statesman in chains. His red hat crowned long service. His conclave vote shaped the papacy.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-basilica: A 1913 entry on the basilica — the church's ancient form. Gerhard Gietmann traces its Roman roots. The long nave leads to the apse. The Christians took the law court's shape. The architecture of the early Church. Its plan shaped a thousand churches.
